summary: Sand Hill fire tower near Massena, St. Lawrence County: 80 ft Aermotor LS-40 from about 1950, officially closed 1959, removed about 1961; only footers seen in 2012.

facts.design: Aermotor LS-40 steel fire tower with observer's cabin
facts.status_note: Officially closed in 1959 and removed around 1961; only the footers for the tower and cabin remained when the DEC plan recorded the site in 2012.

access.note: Roadside site on State Highway 420, across from the Norfolk fire station. Only footers remain; the DEC plan describes the site as of 2012.

visit.trail_note: Roadside site per the DEC unit plan. Only footers remain to see.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: An April 1950 paper says the station was started the year before, which reads as 1949. Starr's list gives 1950 for the tower's build and first-use year. The story reports both and does not pick one.

notes_for_editor: Thin record: one newspaper item, one compiled list and one DEC plan. The 1949/1950 start is a real disagreement and is reported in the story. The DEC plan's 2012 footers observation is the latest source; nothing describes the site after 2012. The access level 'public' is an inference from the roadside location on State Highway 420 in a DEC plan; the plan does not state a visitor status. Staffing value 'emergency' is a best fit for 'operated by fire wardens on a need by need basis'. No photos found; no photo search within budget.
